en: One Scroll of the Yoga Lotus Family Recitation Method.
Compiled by Kai-fu Yi-tong San-si, Te-jin, Shi Hong-lu-qing, Duke of Su with a Fief of Three Thousand Households,
conferred purple robes, posthumously titled司空 (Sikong) and Grand Master of Great Enlightenment (Da Jian).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Temple, who bears the title "Great and Vast Wisdom," by imperial decree.
Having first entered the maṇḍala and performed the wholehearted prostrations, confessions, vows, and dedications of merit;
Then, form the mudrā of the joined palms of the lotus: let the two hands be hollow with the palms resembling unopened lotus petals,
while reciting the mantra of the purity of all phenomena.
Recite [the mantra] once each at the heart, forehead, throat, and crown;
one will immediately attain purification.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvabhāvātmaka sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśuddho ’haṃ. Then, placing the right knee on the ground, join the palms in the lotus gesture (padmāñjali) and place them upon the crown of the head.
Recite the mantra while visualizing paying homage at the feet of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and *iṣṭadevatās*.
The mantra is: Oṃ padma-mūrdhe. Having performed this rite, [proceed].
Thereupon, one fully accomplishes the rites of prostration, service, and offering to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
thereafter, one sits in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka) or the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka).
Then, one forms the Lotus Samaya-mudrā:
with both hands, interlace the fingers outwardly in the gesture of palms joined;
extend the two thumbs and the two little fingers, keeping them parallel to one another.
Present this to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and deities (iṣṭadevatā).
They will immediately remember their original vows and grant their empowerment and protection.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadmasamayas tvaṃ. Next, bind the Seal of Supreme Joy (*paramānanda-mudrā*), following the same hand gestures as before.
Simply take the two middle fingers and let them hang down into the palms,
with the nail-faces of the fingers joined together.
The mantra is: Oṃ samaya hūḥ sara-ta-satvaṃ. Next, form the heart-seal (*hṛdayamudrā*) and visualize it above the two breasts.
The syllable *traṭ* on the right is like a door hinge;
it is opened by performing three pulls with the vajra-bind.
To open one's own mind, it is like lifting a door-panel. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-bandha traṭ. Next, bind the Wisdom-Entry Mudrā (Jñānapraveśa-mudrā).
Perform the previous vajra-bind,
but bend both thumbs into the palms;
visualize a white lotus flower one cubit in front [of you].
Above, place the syllable *Aḥ*, from which white light issues forth;
it flows into the heart and rests upon a white lotus.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajravisphoṭa phaṭ. Next, perform the seal for closing the heart-gate.
It is performed according to the previous binding, but with the two index fingers placed side by side against the joints of the two thumbs.
Touch the heart with that mudrā. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi hūṃ. Then, visualize the gate as closed and next form the *samādhi-mudrā*.
Interlace both hands and place them facing upward beneath the navel;
press the two thumbs together with their tips pointing upward.
Then recite the mantra for entering samādhi as follows:
Oṃ samādhipadmī hrīḥ. Next, one should straighten the body, maintain right mindfulness, and enter *samādhi*.
Resting the tongue against the upper palate, one should bring all discursive thoughts to rest.
Contemplate that all internal and external phenomena are utterly non-existent.
If discursive thoughts are numerous, one should first practice counting the breaths.
The method for counting the breaths proceeds from one breath up to seven breaths.
Furthermore, from one up to seven, the continuity remains uninterrupted.
When the mind is free from objective referents (*ālambana*), there is no need for counting the breaths;
one enters deeply into the sphere of nothingness (*ākiṃcanyāyatana*).
He then visualizes all Buddhas filling the void of space;
their bodies, though as small as sesame seeds, are endowed with all the primary and secondary marks.
They address the practitioner, saying:
"Good son, observe your own mind.
Furthermore, observe your own body as you prostrate yourself, touching the Buddha's feet with your forehead, and say to the Buddha: 'World-Honored One, how does one observe the mind?'"
"What is the characteristic of the mind?
The Buddhas replied,
"Good son, the characteristic of the mind is difficult to measure."
Bestow the mantra for secret recitation and contemplation. The mantra is:
Oṃ citta-prativedhaṃ kuru me. The practitioner should secretly recite this and contemplate their own mind as being like a pure moon.
The Buddhas said:
"Good son, your mind is fundamentally thus;
it is merely obscured by adventitious defilements."
One should know that this is precisely the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, the mantra is bestowed as follows: Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. Recite this mantra.
Contemplate with clarity that the moon of the mind becomes increasingly distinct, pure, and free from all blemishes.
Then, within the lunar disc, visualize the syllable *hrīḥ*,
which transforms into an eight-petaled white lotus, radiating brilliant light.
The mantra is:
Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra padma. Furthermore, one should contemplate this white lotus as pervading the entire dharma-realm, equal in measure to empty space.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvavajrapadma. Next, visualize a white lotus flower that gradually contracts and closes.
All the Buddhas of the void enter therein, their measure equal to one’s own body.
The mantra is: Oṃ saṃhara vajra padma. Immediately, the lotus transforms into the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Adorned with a precious crown, necklaces, and the marks and signs of excellence,
he emits great radiance that pervades the entire Dharma-realm.
Upon his crown is the principal deity Amitāyus, whose left hand holds a white lotus flower.
With the right hand, form the gesture of opening a lotus.
The mantra is: Oṃ samayohana mahāsamayohana sarvatathāgataviṣamodita vajrapadma ātmako 'haṃ. One who enters this samādhi...
All the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings see that the body of the practitioner is equal to that of Avalokiteśvara without distinction;
they are able to eliminate the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated by the practitioner over immeasurable billions of kalpas.
All supreme aspirations shall attain siddhi without exception.
One will immediately realize the perfect Vajradharmakāya;
by contemplating this very body, one attains perfect enlightenment.
Next, perform the empowerment mudrā:
having first formed the vajra-bond by interlacing the fingers outward,
immediately bend the two index fingers.
Hold the two thumbs together.
Recite the mantra once at each of the heart, forehead, throat, and crown.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ hṛīḥ sarvakarādiṣṭhita svāhaṃ. Next, form the consecration mudrā:
join the palms together.
Extend both thumbs upward and curl the remaining eight fingers inward like the shape of a jewel;
place them upon the crown of the head and recite the mantra three times.
Visualize the crowns of the five Tathāgatas adorning one’s head.
The mantra is: Oṃ hṛīḥ maṇi padme abhiṣiñca sarvamaṃ tṛhṛīḥ. Next, bind the garland-seal (mālā-mudrā) and recite the mantra.
First, form the crown-mudrā;
from the forehead, extend two hands which circle three times behind the head like a bound garland.
Then, bring it forward to the side of the ear and let it hang down from the little finger like a garland or sash.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadma māle maṃ hrīḥ. Next, bind the armor mudrā: form the vajra-fist as if a small child were clenching its hands tightly.
Having placed each of the two index fingers against the joint of its respective thumb at the heart,
one then extends the two index fingers so that they overlap for the distance of one joint.
Again, place the right index finger over the left;
visualize the syllable Oṃ on the face of the right index finger and the syllable Taṃ on the face of the left index finger.
One continues to recite these two-syllable mantra words within the mouth without interruption.
One visualizes that both syllables emit green light,
like drawing lotus fibers, with the light stream unbroken.
Circumambulate three times above the heart, three times on the back,
and again at the navel and both knees.
Again, it reaches the waist and then the heart.
Next, it goes to the right shoulder and the left shoulder, then to the top of the forehead.
Having encircled each of these, including the back of the head, three times each:
Next, form the Vajra-fist mudrā and release it from the little fingers as if they were celestial robes hanging down.
Then, with the two hands bound so that they cannot be released,
simply strike them together three times with the palms.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajrapadmaduḥ svāhā. Next, within the maṇḍala, one visualizes the syllable Ā above, which forms a moon disc.
Within the lunar disc, visualize the syllable *hrīḥ* transforming into the body of the principal deity,
emitting great rays of light;
immeasurable retinues appear universally within the circular halo.
Then, form the hook mudrā:
from the vajra-bind, raise the right index finger and beckon three times like a hook.
Recite once and perform one invocation. The mantra is:
Oṃ āya he jvālaya. [Perform] the *pāśa-mudrā*.
As before, bind the two index fingers together so they touch like a ring,
and draw the Honored One into the wisdom-body of the visualized deity.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ hūṃ. Next, form the *śṛṅkhalā-mudrā* (chain seal).
Following the previous method, bind the two index fingers and the two thumbs together;
interlace them so that they press against one another like a linked chain.
Cause the deity to abide. The mantra is:
Oṃ he saḥ phuṭ maṃ. Next, form the bell mudrā.
As before, bind the two thumbs, bending them into the palms;
shake the hands three times like ringing a bell to cause the Honored One to rejoice.
The mantra is: Oṃ viśaye hūṃ. Next, perform the mudrā for offering scented water (argha).
Recite the hundred-syllable mantra or other hymns of praise.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing outward and spread them apart.
Join the tips of the two middle fingers together and slightly bend the two index fingers.
The backs of the middle fingers are separated by the distance of one grain of barley so that they do not touch,
resembling the head of a three-pronged vajra.
The two thumbs are pressed against the lower sides of the two index fingers.
Then, imagining that the palms are filled with fragrant water,
recite the mantra while pouring it forward to wash the feet of the deity.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vairocana gaṭ. Once the principal deity has arrived, next form the karma-mudrā:
place the left hand in a vajra-fist at the heart and visualize a white lotus flower.
The right hand also forms a vajra-fist and is rotated above;
visualize it pushing open the lotus petals.
This is the mantra for the activities of the deity’s body: [Mantra follows]
Oṃ vajradharma hrīḥ. Next, form the samaya-mudrā: with the vajra-bind, bend the two index fingers and press them down with the two thumbs.
Performing the aforementioned empowerment mudrā,
cause the Honored One to recall their original vow and provide empowerment and protection.
The mantra is as follows:
Recite "Oṃ sarvakāri" three times, and then form the mudrā of the inner offering of Vajralāsyā:
perform the vajra-bond, extend both thumbs,
and bend them toward the body, placing them side by side at the heart.
The mantra is: Oṃ mahāratī. To bind the garland, follow the previous mudrā without further alteration.
Simply extend both arms side by side straight forward,
placing them against the forehead.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ lu po śu bhe. Next, form the *gā* mudrā.
Without altering the previous mudrā, release it from the front toward the mouth.
Lowering both hands forward,
as if emitting the sound of a song,
the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ julu-tara-saukhye. Next, bind the dance mudrā: rotate two vajra-fists around each other.

Spread the fingers starting from the little fingers, then perform the vajra-joined palms (vajra-añjali) and place them upon the crown of the head. Regarding the vajra-joined palms: join the palms so that the fingertips are interlaced, with the right hand pressing down on the left. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarva-pūre pūraya. The above constitutes the four inner offerings. Next, form the incense mudrā:
from the vajra-bond, release [the fingers] downward.
As for burning incense, the mantra is: Oṃ praharaṇiṇe. Next, form the flower mudrā.
With the vajra-bind, move upward and release it as if scattering flowers.
The mantra is:
Oṃ phalagami. Next, form the lamp mudrā;
it is performed according to the previous playful gesture, but using the two thumbs.
Bend the heads forward so they press against each other,
yet do not allow the fingers to touch.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sutejagṛhī. Next, form the incense mudrā by releasing the vajra-bond.
Rub it upon the chest in the manner of applying incense; the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ su-gandhe gṛhṇa. The above constitutes the four outer offerings. Next, form the fundamental mudrā of the family-heart:
join the palms and interlace the two ring fingers and the two index fingers.
First, cross the hands. Then,
spread apart the two little fingers and the two thumbs,
and recite the hundred-syllable mantra three times.
After reciting the three-and-a-half-syllable mantra seven times, scatter [the flowers] upon the crown of the head.
Then, holding the rosary, perform the recitation;
grasp the beads with both hands at the level of the heart while reciting.
Contemplate clearly that the Honored One emits pure light,
which flows down and illuminates the moon at the heart;
upon the moon is a white lotus flower.
One’s own body and the form and characteristics of the deity are non-dual;
it is like looking at one's own body in a clear mirror,
where oneself and the deity mutually become reflections of each other.
When the recitation of the full number is completed, perform the repentance and make vows.
Re-present the samaya offerings and re-bind the eight offerings.
Thereafter, dismiss the Honored Ones so that they may return to their original palaces.
To perform the dismissal, one should release [the mudrā] at the mouth using the aforementioned three *samaya*-mudrās. The mantra is:
Oṃ padma-sattva muḥ. Thereafter, one should again form the empowerment, consecration, armor, and slapping (*sphoṭana*) mudrās.
Thereafter, one should exit the maṇḍala.
One may either recite Mahāyāna sūtras or seal the Buddha [image] to create a stūpa.
At all times, do not allow the samādhi of the deity to be interrupted.
If you touch an impure place, you should visualize the syllable *dharmadhātu-janman* (Dhīḥ) upon the crown of your head,
emitting red light.
Regarding the syllable *raṃ*:
one should empower all food with this syllable,
whereby it will not become defiled by contact, even when used for all offerings of incense and flowers.
All [the deities] empower these syllables, emitting white light; thus,
there is no longer any defilement or impurity,
and all offered objects pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
The hundred-syllable mantra of the Padma family is as follows: Oṃ padmasattvasamaya manupālaya padmasattva tvaṃ me.
1. *pattiṣṭha* 2. *nirvṛtiṃ bhava* 3. *santuṣṭiṃ me bhava* 4. *anuraktiṃ me bhava* 5.
*suprasannāṃ me bhava* 6. *sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha*
CAḤ | SARVAKARMASUJE | CITTAŚRĪYE | KURU HŪM | HA HA HA HA HOḤ | BHAGAVAN | SARVATATHĀGATA | PRAMARDANI | MAMA MUNCA | PA... (The text ends here.)
Namaḥ prabhava mahāsamayasattva hriḥ. *The Ritual for Recitation of the Yoga Lotus Family*, one fascicle.
